runtime_status: NOT_MEASURED for clean deployment; available code instruments cache/query/finite/hash/weight witnesses
counting: MAC means one multiply-accumulate; two FLOPs per MAC; main counts exclude elementwise work, narrow feature CAL transforms, Gram/SVD, low-order solves, packing, IO and layout.
notes: The main readout MAC count assumes r=32, k=16 and p=64; actual r_eff and current support may differ. It excludes narrow 32xr CAL transforms and support/solver cost.

Current disk cache writes CPU tensors, fsyncs and hashes after each write; every load validates a full file hash then mmap-loads and transfers to the device. Logical bytes are not measured physical storage bytes because OS page cache matters.
Current query capture, full tensor finite checks, weight witnesses, parameter reads and host synchronizations are research instrumentation.

A full-FFN 64-row observer needs both original W1 and W2, whose BF16 weight payload is 270 MiB per site. Device-resident vs offloaded weights changes cost. A Q1 hit mathematically needs only A and C0; the actual host may still preload original weights.

When all current feature directions are retained, the tall SVD can be removed algebraically by solving the full r-dimensional regularized SPD normal equation. Dropping small nonzero directions changes this statement; replacing SVD by a Gram eigensolve squares conditioning.
Changing to an explicit U0/Y0/Phi0 cache removes anchor U0A but roughly doubles state payload; this changes BF16 delta/cache rounding and is not an exact native-program rewrite.
The online path alone executes observer/support/SVD/adapter; the static arm does not. Both arms execute the full Nxd readout projection and output combination.

Current eager _deployed adds full Nxd BF16 materialization, FP32 casts and sum. The separate-operation output-related logical access is 32*N*d bytes per hit; it is not measured HBM traffic. A fused epilogue must preserve the intermediate BF16 projection rounding to retain the old numerical semantics.

Dense anchor already computes full z/h, but replacing the current narrow Phi0 with selected full-GEMM columns may change BF16 projection rounding relative to the narrow hit endpoint. The N*d*k saving is a conditional small optimization, not automatically an equivalent rewrite.
